findings.description: Location seven, lint-scope.sh:2-5 (the file's opening description). Shipped: "Walk one opted-in scope and check every v2 note and record against the machine contracts in references/machine-contracts.md. The walk takes in v1 files as well, checking their wiki links and nothing else: a link resolves against every file in the scope, and that resolution never reads the file's own frontmatter." Decided by :427 (the one loop over the whole scope glob), :434-441 (a file with no schema key is pushed onto v1_files, its body cached, and `continue`s out of pass two), and :491-495 (the v1 pass, whose body is check_links and nothing else). The named lines make the sentence true rather than false, and the claim was corrected rather than deleted: the file still opens by stating what it walks and what each generation receives.
findings.evidence: inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh:2-5 (claim). Deciding lines, quoted from the shipped file: :427 `for file in "$scope"/notes/*.md "$scope"/_memory/*/*.md "$scope"/entries/*.md; do`; :434-441 `if ! has_schema_key "$file"; then / v1=$((v1 + 1)) / v1_files+=("$file") / ... / continue / fi`; :491-495 `for file in ${v1_files[@]+"${v1_files[@]}"}; do / index=$((index + 1)) / current_file="$file" / check_links "${v1_body_for_index[$index]}" / done`. The retained first clause "check every v2 note and record" is true against :443 `v2_files+=("$file")` feeding the full check set at :452-475.

findings.description: Location seven's two subordinate factual claims are also true. "a link resolves against every file in the scope" and "that resolution never reads the file's own frontmatter" are both decided by check_links at :372-386, which resolves a target with `find "$scope" -name ...` over the whole scope and touches no frontmatter of the linking file at any point.
findings.evidence: inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh:381-383 `find "$scope" -name "$target.md" -print -quit | grep -q . && continue` / `local id="${target: -10}"` / `find "$scope" -name "*$id*.md" -print -quit | grep -q . && continue`. check_links' only input is the extracted body path "$1" (:386 `done < <(grep -oE '\[\[[^]|]*' "$1" ...)`), and extract_body stops at the fence, so no frontmatter is read.

findings.description: Location eight, lint-scope.sh:416-422 (above pass one). Shipped: "Pass one classifies and caches each v2 body, because the resolution and recurrence checks are scope-wide: they can't be answered from inside one file. It caches v1 bodies too, for a narrower reason. Only the link pass at the bottom of the file reads them, and this is the one loop that visits every file, so extracting here costs one walk instead of two. They go to their own `body.v1.*` files and never join `open-slugs`, which is what keeps a v1 question out of the two scope-wide checks." Decided by :439 (v1 bodies extracted here), :494 (the sole read of v1_body_for_index), and :448 (open-slugs written only in the v2 branch, after the v1 `continue` at :440). The claim was extended, not deleted.
findings.evidence: inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh:416-422 (claim). Deciding lines: :438-439 `v1_body_for_index[$v1_index]="$work/body.v1.$v1_index"` / `extract_body "$file" >"$work/body.v1.$v1_index"`; :494 `check_links "${v1_body_for_index[$index]}"`. Every reference to open-slugs in the file: $ grep -n "open-slugs" inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh -> 414 (init), 421 (this comment), 448 (write, inside the v2 branch), 480 (open-question-resolution), 488, 508 (RECURRING). The write at :448 is unreachable for a v1 file because :440 `continue`s first, and the only two consumers are :480 and :508 -- exactly the "two scope-wide checks" the comment names.

findings.description: Locations one through six were not re-opened. The two lint-scope.sh locations T-003 shipped are byte-identical to the text its checker quoted, shifted only by the lines T-004 added above them: the header comment (T-003 verdict: :10-15, now :12-17, +2) and the pass-two comment (T-003 verdict: :451-457, now :458-464, +7). Neither appears as a changed line attributable to T-004 in the diff. The four documentation locations are in files T-004 did not touch.
findings.evidence: T-003's checker quoted the header as "The only check here that touches a v1 file is the link check. Files without a `schema` key predate the contract, they stay legal indefinitely... Links stay on because a target that resolves to no file in scope is broken whichever generation wrote it, and verify-migration.sh already runs that same resolution over the whole scope without ever reading `schema`." -- character-for-character what now stands at inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh:12-17. Same for the pass-two comment at :458-464, "Links stay on either way, and they run on files with no `schema` key too, in the pass below: ... carries none of them for a count to be compared against." The offset map is fully consistent: every line T-003's verdict cited above 418 is now +2 (:13-15->:15-17, :23-24->:25-26, :379-381->:381-383) and every line below is now +7 (:427-434->:434-441, :449->:456, :451-457->:458-464, :458-465->:465-472, :466->:473, :468->:475, :484-488->:491-495, :487->:494). Two insertions, no in-place edits, nothing else moved.

findings.description: Every line T-004 changed is comment text; no line of code changed. `git diff -- inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh` is +39/-6 in total, and every changed line is attributable to exactly one of three tasks. T-001 contributed 19 pure insertions, all code; T-003 contributed +12/-5, all comment; the remaining +8/-1 is T-004's, and it is two comment blocks.
findings.evidence: $ git diff --stat -- inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh -> 1 file changed, 39 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-). T-001's 19 code lines, each confirmed by T-001's own checker verdict quoting them: `declare -a v1_body_for_index=()` (1); `v1_files=()` and `v1_index=0` (2); the four caching lines at :436-439 (4); the v1 pass block :490-495 plus its blank line and 5-line comment (12). T-003's +12/-5: header hunk +6/-3 and pass-two comment +6/-2, both quoted verbatim in T-003's verdict. Residual = +8/-1, which is exactly hunk one's `-# contracts in references/machine-contracts.md.` replaced by three comment lines (:3-5), and the five comment lines at :418-422. Both begin with `#`. No `+` or `-` line outside those two blocks lacks a T-001 or T-003 attribution, so no code line is T-004's.

findings.description: Both rewritten comments carry the reason alongside the rule, in the file's own register, and break neither typographic rule. No sentence in either block states a rule with no reason attached.
findings.evidence: Reason-bearing clauses, quoted: :4-5 "checking their wiki links and nothing else: a link resolves against every file in the scope, and that resolution never reads the file's own frontmatter" -- the rule (links only) with the reason (link resolution is generation-blind) in the same sentence. :418-420 "It caches v1 bodies too, for a narrower reason. Only the link pass at the bottom of the file reads them, and this is the one loop that visits every file, so extracting here costs one walk instead of two." :421-422 "never join `open-slugs`, which is what keeps a v1 question out of the two scope-wide checks." Register matches the surrounding comments at :7-10, :368-371, and :485-489, all of which explain a constraint rather than restate the code. Typographic scan over both blocks: $ sed -n '2,5p;416,422p' inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh | grep -n ' \u2014 \|\*\*[^*]*:\*\*' -> exit 1, no match; $ ... | grep -c '\u2014' -> 0. No bolded inline header, no em dash at all, so none wrapped in spaces.
